state:
**Goal `path-literals-follow-up`: Stages 1 to 5 are on disk, and Stage 6's compiler half is on disk.** Stage 1's floor is goal `plain-comments`'s list.

ADR 0250 is written: it `modifies` `rule:types/class-reference` (which states the rule) and `rule:programs/no-runtime-autoload` (one pointer sentence). A plain string literal under `as class<T>` or `as ?class<T>` is the class's whole name (`nvs_hir::QName::from_literal`), `nvs_hir::requires`' harvest loads it through `autoload`, and `nvs-types` reports `E0303` or `E0708` for it. `nvs-ir` writes the descriptor as a constant. The four `nvs-types` tests, the `nvs-hir` test and the three `.nvst` cases of Stage 6 pass.

Two existing programs used a literal naming no class to reach the run-time throw. The hostile attack `tests/hostile/lang/classes/inheritance/01-a-chain-that-never-ends-and-a-class-name-that-is-not-one.nvs` and the conformance case `the-php-differences-files-tags-and-names-rows-run-as-written.nvst` now build that name at run time.

Still red in Stage 6: `nvs-lsp-a-class-literal-completes-every-loadable-class`.

Stage 4's example 01 (`docs/examples/core/Path/fromCwd/01-a-file-name-from-the-command-line.nvs`) is still only half done: it does not read the file, because the example runner gives no `fs.read` grant at the repository root.

`bun nv proofs --id` reads the roster from a stale `nvs` unless you pass `--nvs` (playbook, Tooling).
